hypothesis: Non-symplectic integrators drift in the first integrals of the geodesic flow (speed, Clairaut constant, angular momentum); adaptive local-error control accumulates a linear secular drift, while a fixed step on these closed or quasi-periodic orbits can keep the speed drift bounded over long stretches; bounded speed error does not guarantee the right orbit.
input_data: Torus(2, 1) start (0, 0.5) heading 0.7 (bounded oscillation about the outer equator)
Fixed step h = 0.125 for Euler, midpoint, RK4; DP45 rtol 1e-06, atol 1e-09; checkpoints L = 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320
mathematical_model: Energy g(v, v) = 1, torus Clairaut rho^2 phi' and sphere angular momentum M = X x X' are exact first integrals. On the unit sphere |M| is the speed and M/|M| the normal of the orbit plane, so a position error splits into a cross-track part, bounded by the tilt of M/|M|, and an along-track (phase) part. A speed error advances the point along its circle by the integrated excess arclength int (|X'| - 1) ds; a speed error growing ~ L therefore gives along-track error ~ L^2 (adaptive DP45). A tilt of the orbit plane growing ~ L gives cross-track error ~ L (fixed-step RK4, whose local error rotates the plane secularly while its speed error stays bounded). On Torus(2, 1) the orbit oscillates between |theta| <= arccos((c - R)/r); a Clairaut drift across the separatrix changes it into an orbit winding around the tube.
numerical_result: Energy exponents: adaptive torus 0.934, sphere 0.998; RK4 envelope exponent 0.0275 (torus, L = 10-160) and 0.00661 (sphere, L = 10-320), torus RK4 local slope 0.861 from L = 160 to 320; sphere position exponent RK4 1.02, adaptive 2.05; at L = 320 the RK4 position error 0.000541 is cross-track 0.000541 (orbit-plane tilt 0.000546, tilt exponent 1.01), its along-track part -2.6e-05 has the opposite sign to the integrated speed error 0.00016; the adaptive position error 0.0102 is along-track -0.01021 against an integrated speed error -0.01023; torus adaptive Clairaut exponent 0.999 over L = 40-320 (local slopes 1.33, 1.16, 0.928, 1.05, 0.999); fixed-step Clairaut envelopes are not described by one exponent (local slopes: Euler 1.3, 0.82, 0.5, 0.11, 0.0047, RK4 0.18, 0.23, 0.43, 0.57, 0.74); torus Euler max energy error 0.035 but max |theta| 285 versus turning latitude 1.369; sphere Euler stopped at s = 14.
observation_model: Running maxima (envelopes) of |I(s) - I(0)| at checkpoints; exponents are log-log slopes over the reached checkpoints; no renormalization at any step.

title: Explore long-horizon numerical drift.
uncertainty: Envelope exponents mix oscillatory and secular parts, so single-exponent fits are reported only where the local slopes agree; the torus RK4 energy local slopes are 0, 0, 0, 0.14, 0.86 over L = 10-320, so its secular part appears between L = 160 and 320 and may dominate beyond; the adaptive torus Clairaut slopes settle only from L = 40, so its exponent is fitted there. Fits use the six checkpoints or the stated subrange. The sphere position decomposition is linear in errors below 0.01 (RK4 and adaptive), so second-order cross terms are negligible.
unresolved_assumptions: Two geodesics only; resonant or chaotic geodesics are not sampled
Horizon 320 is limited by the run budget; asymptotic drift laws are not established
